betterquesting:10.desc:8: The Rocket you landed in can definitely not make another trip, it's for the best if you disassemble it and recycle the scraps. Please take cover when you do, though. I don't trust §6Izawa §fto have made it any more stable than absolutely necessary, so treat it like it's rigged to explode.
Using a §dSkyhook§f, you can ride along Powerlines. Rope, steel cable, etc. also work. simply right-click with it while near a wire.

§dStation Markers§f can be renamed via right-click. 
Clicking on a Station with a §dTicket§f §fwill add it to its schedule. Clicking on a Locomotive will apply said schedule to it. 

Here's where the magic happens: If a valid path across the rail network is found, a train with a schedule will be directed towards its next destination by having tracks on T-Junctions always curve in the direction needed.
§cNote: this does not work with Railcraft's junctions. However, all its track types are still compatible.

§fTo look up your entire train network, you can make a §dTrain Network Controller§f to see all tracks, station names and trains moving throughout it.
Using some of the leftover petals, we can make floral powder and steep that in mana to create a potent substance with all kinds of interesting properties!

Tired of manually calibrating timers and counters, logic gates taking up half your real estate? Then you'll love our new and §dimproved Logic Gates§f made from quartz and red alloy. they can be chiselled into whatever circuit you need. §6NAND, AND, XOR, Timers, Latches, §fand even some §6sensors§f,whatever your heart desires. 

Like red alloy wire, you can put these on walls and the ceiling, aswell as have multiple in the same blockspace.
These things' insides look like a horribly mutated form of lung tissue. I suspect it's some kind of metabolic organ.
A direct upgrade to the Crossbow Turret. It sports faster firing rate aswell as an adjustable target filter.

These Tentacles are mostly made up of muscly tendrils, but the tip houses what appears to be various primitive eyes and olfactory receptors. I suspect it acts as a fortified sensory organ, allowing the Infection to sense intruders easier. This hypothesis is supported by its primary form of attack, which is sprouting smaller tendrils from surrounding infected ground.

I hope these tiny flying critters didn't cause you too much trouble. They sport tiny stingers that inject a muscle relaxant, weakening your attacks.

If you want to prevent more from spawning, it is advised to keep any and all §6Trees§f out of tainted Territory.
Ok, so let me get this straight. you made a book with some petals and a zombie brain and now it just has... fully legible writing in it? in our language? I'm going to need a copy of this.

betterquesting:10.name:8: Not that big of a Fan...
betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Conveyors are practical for precise item transport, but sometimes you need to collect things from a wide area or places where the ground needs to be exposed. Fortunately, §5Dr. Xavier §flet me tinker with those flowers a bit, and i think i've come up with something. 

I'll be the first to admit that it's far from optimal, but this §dDaffomill§f uses a small amount of mana to push items on the ground in the direction it is facing.

In order to better understand the nature of this "Taint", you should gather samples of biomass. 

Most of these shoud be easily obtainable from infected creatures, though in a pinch some of the tainted blocks can drop them aswell.

So turns out all this purple smoke you've been haphazardly dumping into the atmosphere is the nutrients the Taint has been waiting for all this time. When the pollution reaches it, it will try to infect any and all soil between it and its food source- your factory.
However, I have good news: In order to digest pollution, the Taint sprouts Taint Seeds which are quite fragile compared to the rest of the biomass. it should be easy enough for ranged weaponry to take care of them. I suspect that you won't just stop polluting, however. go ask §7Lieutenant Briggs§f if she can set you up with some automated defenses.

What in the- this stuff is completely different to all life as we know it. Fungi and slime molds come close, but it also shares molecules with §osilicone rubber and lead paint§f of all things, aswell as some as of yet unidentified compounds.
There's no way something like this evolved here naturally, it feels out of place even in this biosphere.

From what i could tell it also has no metabolism to speak of. As if it was lying dormant, waiting for new food to appear. Whatever that may be.

It will infect nearby living creatures however, presumably to defend itself in an energy-efficient 
manner.

While it is possible to run around the area with a thaumometer like a maniac, it is certainly not avised. If you consult your fullscreen map, there is a setting called §6Toggle Aura/Flux Display§f on the right. If this is active, any §dThaumic Dioptras§f in Flux Mode will broadcast the current §5§lFlux §flevel in their scanning area (13x13 chunks) to any Agents that have interacted with it.

The Pollution Overlay will not update automatically, but closing and re-opening the fullscreen map will refresh it.

Maybe §6killing off those Taint Seeds§f wasn't such a bright idea afterall... This stuff §6adapts rather quickly the more you try to hold it off like this§f. It can already infect solid rock, I don't think i want to know what else it's capable of if you keep going.
Ok, i'm a biologist, of course I would want to know... but maybe from a bit more distance.

I don't think it's avoidable though. Best course of action would probably be to §6look into ways to reduce pollution§f.

First scans show that much of the plantlife here is very familiar- grass, trees, flowers, you name it. However, there are a few that stick out. Would you mind breaking some for examination? Whether you get them back intact does not matter.

Note: any Mystical Flower will work

These flowers are extraordinary! They emit faint beta radiation and have an otherwise unnatural sparkle to them that I can't quite describe. Mind sending some samples? Some fertilizer would also be neat so we can propagate them up here. Most animals here drop bones when killed, so getting some shouldn't be an issue.

This Digital Interface lets you communicate with us Researchers and the crew at large. 
Together with your Map and "World Analysis Interpretive Lexicographical Agent" (WAILA), it is part of a small suite of tools we managed to get to the surface with you unscathed.


Why don't you check whether the scanner is working and send us a piece of dirt?
So this Fern isn't particularly notable in the paranormal sense. However, it only grows on top of §6§dClay§f. Might be worth keeping in mind when looking for it.

Crops only grow in certain climates, check whether they are growing and the climate info when hovering over the item.

If a crop gets too far outside its temperature range, it can die.
No Description

If you do not wish to engage with trains, Collins told me there's something in this Thaumonomicon called "§dMagic Mirrors§f". Might be worth loking into. Though they also said §6something about it destabilizing local spacetime, creating §5§lFlux§6 at both end points§f. Still sounds better than dealing with signals though, amirite?

Ok so you won't believe this, but I just went to wash the petals you sent and somehow they spontaneously fused into... this? It does look mildly more useful than the other flowers by themselves.


Let's see if you can replicate the process. A stone basin filled with water should be enough. Throw in some petals in a valid combination aswell as a seed to finish it.Looks like it just ate my lead crystal seeds so it should really not matter what type.
The very first Flower you should make. Don't ask me how fusing 4 petals of the same color results in an entirely new plant, or how it can transform blocks in the world around itself.

In order to guarantee fully automatic flower production, this thing is a must. i tried feeding it with some mana i squeezed from a hydroangeas and it immediately started extending its roots, sprouting more mystical flowers around itself!

A horn of the wild can produce a strong enough gust to uproot them, but that's a bit manual. Maybe we could apply the same principles to a drum or something?

Only downside is that i have yet to find a way to make it only produce the colors we want instead of a homogenous mix of everything...

A busy industrialist like you will certainly not want to entertain the idea of having to stop automating just to forage for some food. Fortunately, this mana powder makes for some very filling flour substitute.

But while its §6Caloric Value§f might be immense, this stuff has §6next to no Nutritional Value§f.
This flower is brimming with nutrients and is willing to share them with any plants around, provided you feed it some mana as compensation.

In order to get raw Stone, you will need to carve it out of the rock: Whenever you mine all 6 cardinal neighbors of a stone block, it will pop right off.

If you want to get chiseled/smooth stone instead, you can left-click it with a §dChisel§f in hand and then mine it directly.

In case you're having trouble getting Redstone, I somehow managed to fuse several redstone roots and red petals into a flower that can renewably leech it from redstone ore. To create redstone ore, simply expose a redstone block to a pure daisy.

§cProbably gonna be replaced by sth requiring cinnabar/cryolite at some point

§fThe Agricarnation works wonders on these §dRed Orchids§f, so growing them at a good rate shouldn't pose any issues. it is noteworthy that their deep roots prevent them from being harvested by the drum of the wild or similar, but other, more standard methods may still work.

This flower is strangely shaped like a hand of sorts and will attempt to place any blocks you feed it in item form around itself, on the block you specify. This is done by placing said block below the dirt the flower is planted on. I recommend using the floating version of the flower, that way it can directly be placed on the block in question.

Some devices have too many variables for a comparator to keep track of. The §dBarrel §ffor instance features both a fluid and item buffer, aswell as the signal the comparator actually winds up outputting which is whether the barrel is sealed or not.

This is where §dDials §fcome in. chiselled from some §dBrass Mechanisms§f, they can be used to relay specific types of information to comparators attached to them. This even allows for §6reading of containers that do not have built-in comparator support§f like individual clothesline anchors or mini chests. Other dial Types can query the fill level of fluid tanks or the speed of Mechanical devices.

§dLight Sensors§f, made by chiselling a §dNAND Gate§f, will by default detect both block and skylight. §6You can cycle through its modes by shift-clicking with a screwdriver§f. Blue means skylight only, red means block light only. §6Useful for devices that emit light or create light-emitting blocks during operation.§f

The §dScanner §fis a versatile device capable of §6reading the Blockstate§f of whereever its "eye" is pointing and emits a redstone signal if it matches the criteria listed in its GUI.

§fAwesome, with Iron and Jute in hand, we can now create §dClotheslines§f. These jute ropes can be used to link §dClothesline Anchors§f, forming a loop that can transport items.

Keep in mind that at least one Anchor must be powered using §6Mechanical Power§f (speed 5.0R or more) Adding more power will speed it up, but it caps out at ~40R.
Anchors can only accept mechanical power from a block they are directly attached to, and only if they are facing either up or down.

Anchors can be interacted with like regular inventories, but will act like they can only hold 1 item. They will also attempt to auto-output to the block they are attached to.

The notable benefit of these compared to conveyors is that they are easier to set up and expand. They also go both ways, so every point on the line can be in- or output. Lastly, Clotheslines will get saturated and stop accepting items if all outputs are full. Contrary to conveyor belts which will happily let any excess accumulate on the final belt segment without additional redstone control.

An annoying caveat is that in order to connect two anchors, §6you have to hold down right-click while dragging your cursor from one to the other§f.

§dConveyor Belts§f are the simplest way of getting items from A to B.
There's several variants that can all be cycled through using the §dChisel§f. 

A §dHammer§f is able to rotate them in any of the 4 cardinal directions. Shift-clicking makes it slope up or down.

Trains are the go-to way of transporting goods across long distances, like from a §6distant resource outpost§f to your main base. 

In order for your trains to work, they will need 3 things:

-A §dLocomotive§f needs to be filled with water (from something like a fluid loader) and solid fuel such as alumentum and will pull the train without any need for pricy booster tracks. Its speed can be set either manually in its GUI or through certain types of track.

-A §dcargo section. §fThis can be anything from crates and fluid wagons to mana pools.
For some reason, Ship Command has disallowed putting regular chests or TNT into carts. Treated wood crates should work just fine though.

-A §dWorldspike Cart §fensures that the train remains properly supervised. i don't know what exactly this entails, but §bCollins§f said it had something to do with how quantum mechanics behaves differently here and almost nothing will work unless observed.

Lastly, use a §dCrowbar§f while sneaking to link the carts together into a train.

§dInserters§f are sort of like hoppers, but better looking, faster, and horizontal.

They will transfer any matching items from their input side (where the arm is pointing when idle) and transfer it to the opposite side. They are peculiar in this in that they can interact with inventories §6both at their Level and one block below, both in-and output,§f though they will usually bind to the first valid target they find. (so you cannot input from 2 chests at once, for instance)

when transferring "diagonally" like this, they ignore any solid blocks in the way. This property makes them very useful on §6flying machines§f where every block counts.

Inserters have a §6wide range of filtering options§f and can §6pick up/ drop off items in-world§f. This, too, works if the items are one block below.

Inserters also §6interact with minecarts just like hoppers§f would, making for aesthetically pleasing train stations.

Their only downside is that they cannot be shut off using redstone.

§dFaucets §fand §dCasting Channels§f are the simplest form of fluid transport. Their throughput is quite limited and they cannot move liquids vertically upwards. 

A Faucet will, if given a redstone signal, pour any liquid from the block it's attached to into the container below. Should this process stall, either because of the input draining completely or the output filling up, it requires another signal. 

Channels have a very limited throughput of ~36 mb/t total.

Copper is a decently ductile material for making, well, §dDucts§f. 
These pipes, due to their closed-top nature, have the ability to be pressurized to allow for virtually unlimited throughput. However, valves at the in- and outlets mean that the Throughput §6Per Connection (aka interfacing with machines and tanks, but not other ducts) §fis limited.

Furthermore, thermal stress is a serious concern with these pipes, and as such they will rupture if made to transfer very hot or cold liquids.

§dServos§f can be attached to Inlets to automatically extract fluid if the machine does not output automatically already. by default they need a redstone signal to activate, but you can change this in its GUI.

Steel is robust enough to allow for some truly heinous valve trickery. these §dPipes§f have no internal buffer and instead relay fluids directly to their destination. §6This makes it possible to have multiple fluid types flowing through the same pipe. §f

These pipes work for any temperature fluid.
however, the Speed is fairly limited unless using §dMechanical or Electric Pumps§f between segments.

§TThe Internal mechanisms require outside pressure to not fluctuate too rapidly, say, through §3High Wind Speeds§f.

A pricey upgrade to the Copper Ducts.
These Pipes can transfer unlimited amounts of liquid of any temperature, now also unrestricted by ports.

Fluids can be moved from Tank to Tank just fine, but when it comes to picking them up from a Puddle in the world, this method breaks down. Usually this can be remedied by giving a bucket to a dispenser, but I can tell you are yearning for something simpler. 

Enter: the §dMechanical Pump§f! 

§e§fTo set it up, configure the in- and outputs using your hammer and apply a redstone signal.
if you are using this for extracting fluids that renew themselves or get placed in the world via automation, I recommend shift-clicking the top with a hammer to stop it from replacing blocks with cobblestone.

the §6Blue Port §fon the top is used for §6Mechanical Power Input§f.
As with other machinery of this type, the §6Mechanical Power from your axles must be fed through a transmission box first§f to serve as a sort of "Adapter".

usually transmission boxes are connected to machines like pumps via §dMotor Belts and Wheels§f, but a direct connection is also possible. §c


Right now there is a bug where devices like the pump stop working after a short while if you directly connect it to the transmission box. I recommend using belts in between. if you insist on using a direct connection, you can also force it to update again by varying the mechanical power you apply, like by briefly cutting it every few seconds.

§dGolems§f are useful for many things, chief among them being item transport and sorting.

Seals such as §dProvide§f, §dStock§f, and §dEmpty§f/§dStore§f do not even require any special components beyond the most basic golem variant.

If you want to increase their speed, consider making them from §6light materials§f and giving them §6Wheels for Legs§f using the various selectors in the Golem Press.
add the fact that golems can carry up to 2 stacks at a time, and you will find that on shorter distances, they can reach remarkable throughput numbers this way.

However, be warned that golems are still somewhat alive and unpredictable, even without misappropriated zombie brains inside. As such it is advisable to assume Murphy's Law:
§6If there is even the slightest chance for a golem to get itself killed or stuck, it will find it.§f 
Make sure to child-proof your golem setups and encase them with solid walls or §dBarrier Stones§f.

If this is not possible for whatever reason, make sure to make your golems in a way where they can handle the environment they are deployed in, like by making them §6fire-or blastproof §fshould they encounter those hazards, or giving them §6flight/climbing legs§f if the terrain is unwieldy.
No Description
The Arcane Grappler, when charged with Vis, can be used to swing around like some sort of man-spider. Very useful for traversing rough terrain.

§dViaducts §fare a more sophisticated way of Infrastructure-guided personal transport. simply create a network of ducts and use a crescent hammer on any end points that you want to designate as a station. 


if you wish to get around faster, §dLong Range Viaducts§f are your friend, though the require a bit more setup.

Firstly, they do not work on their own, but rather connect two ends comprised of regular Viaducts.

The long-range versions cannot branch: If you wish to make a "travel hub" that connects multiple long-range connections, the junction will have to be made from regular Viaducts.

To set up a long-range connection, §dLinking Viaducts§f have to be placed at the transition between duct types. once both ends have been built, update one of the linking ducts via right-click.
We both know you've been waiting for this
No Description
No Description
A collection of entries relating to mostly quality of life. From how to get around faster to easier building and storage systems, I got it all.

Mechanical Power is tansferred primarily via §dAxles§f. They can pnly go straight and cannot split, however, so §dGearboxes §fand §dMergeboxes§f need to be added at junctions and turns.

§dGearboxes§f have one input (denoted by the Strip with 2 arrows facing inward) and 5 outputs. A gear has to be inserted on every side you want to use, including the output. 


When more than one output is attached to a gearbox, the power will be split evenly. This system has no concept of Torque or Stress! Any axles terminating in dead ends will draw just as much power as under full load. It is also excedingly hard to split off exact ratios.

The §dMergebox§f can unify 2 or more inputs into 1 output, provided they spin at the exact same speed and do not rapidly fluctuate.
§f

This Multiblock is able to house planters of crops and fruit trees without them having the chance to die off. it also grows them slightly faster. 

§cThis thing's placement conditions are so contrived that i'm not even gonna try. please go to §2§1§bhttps://github.com/eerussianguy/firmalife/wiki/Greenhouses §cfor example images + explanation.

Sometimes, moving blocks whole is the only viable way to solve a particular problem.

To make this easier, we have devised a couple utilities for you to try and expand the capabilities of pistons and slime blocks:

§dForce Relays §fcan be bound to non-TileEntity blocks using a wand of the forest. when pushed by a piston, the bound block will move aswell. if the force relay is pushed or pulled by a sticky piston, it has no effect on the bound block, making it very easy to make a block "run along" a straight line.

§dColored Slime Blocks§f act independently and will slide past one another.

§dGlazed Trracotta§f is an interesting blockset. it can be pushed by pistons, but its smoothness means it will not stick to slime or sticky pistons trying to pull on it.

§dBlock Signals §fcan be placed on the side of a track to denote a §6Railway Block§f. should a Block already contain a Train, the signal will turn red.

When holding Tracks or signal-related items, the Blocks will show as differently colored strips along the track, along with the direction trains are able to pass in.

§dChain Signals §fAct the same way Block Signals do, but they also turn red if the signal in the Block before it is red.

Signals emit a redstone signal when green, but only to their immediate left, aka into the track they're attached to. Coupled with a §6§dLocking Track Kit§f Locomotives will automatically stop if the signal is red. To prevent Trains from freezing up, it is advised to add a §dDetector Track Kit §fafter the signal so the Locking track stays unlocked as long as there's more wagons passing over it.

Items can be loaded and unloaded with §dInserters§f no problem, but Fluids and other types of cargo need special equipment.

§dFluid Loaders/Unloaders§f go above and below a track, respectively and will fill/ drain the cart below. its GUI also features a Cart filter so you don't accidentally drain your steam locomotives. it also features a configurable redstone output mode.
Similar devices exist for items and electricity.

Mana can also be transported via minecart, and must be inserted and extracted using a §dMana Pump§f. Care must be taken however as the pump will sometimes spill excess mana.

§dTracks§f can be made from just a bit of iron and concrete. To place large amounts of them, especially in straight lines, i recommend a Building Gadget or its copy-paste counterpart.

§dTrack Kits§f can all be chiselled from the Activator variant and modify tracks in various ways. 

It is also possible to use Steel to make §dReinforced Tracks§f which are 25% faster and blast resistant.
If you're in a real hurry, you can even opt to use §dHigh Speed §fRails. However, they cannot take turns and need to be transitioned to and from with grace.
No Description

I have run some experiments on the §dPink Dust§f you made, and it turns out that with some finesse, you can use it to take care of your §5§dstorage system§f!

Place regular §dCorporea Sparks§f above any containers you want to link to the network. Each network also requires a §dMaster Spark§f to orchestrate everything. The master spark cannot take items from its inventory, so best place it above an index or similar. 

The §dCorporea Index§f is where things get interesting. You can request items from your network using either §a§6Chat §for §6By Pressing C over an item in JEI §fwhile in its range. §6Pressing shift + C requests a stack.


§6§5§4§d

§dPortable §fTanks are a fairly simplistic way of storing fluids. they accept it from any side and can auto-output to the bottom if configured to do so using a §dCrescent Hammer§f. Their fill level can be read with comparators, but they do not interface with items. they retain their contents when broken.

§dMultiblock Tanks§f can hold more fluid and can also be used to directly fill and empty buckets and other container items. The smallest one is made of a hollow 3x4x3 cuboid of Tank Wall. non-edge blocks can also be swapped for strengthened glass or tank valves.
No Description
No Description
No Description
No Description

§1Weller §ffound that there's lots of enchanted tomes in the ruins around here! The Lexicon speaks of a way to apply them to equipment without consuming the books. What do you say? want to build a mana enchanter?
For now we don't have many tools at our disposal that would help us with metalworking. I suppose a couple ceramics would be a start.
No Description

I have come up with a way to extract useable quicklime from mana powder using a specialized furnace. Unfortunately, this requires boiling off some of the other paranormal components, releasing them into the atmosphere. Nothing to worry about, i'm sure.

I would advise you to put a chimney on that thing though.

With a jaded amaranth flower farm and pasture seeds under our belt, I think there's nothing preventing us from making as many hydroangeas as we want and automatically replace any that decay! Way better than those stupid endoflames that need manual intervention. this could be fully automatic!

The Petal apothecary can be given water by dropping a full bucket on it, returning an empty one. It can be filled again either via dispenser or by infusing it with mana.

Pointing one of these spreaders at a pool makes it slowly accumulate mana that we can soak certain items in to convert them by dropping them in.

For instance, throwing in some petals will cause them to grow into straw, and throwing that in again yields pasture seeds.

The latter is particularly interesting because it counts as a valid seed for the Apothecary. Bygone are the days of needing to sacrifice valuable crop seeds to make flowers!
No Description

These Silverwood Trees are a peculiar bunch. No, not because of the whole "Aura Replenishing" thing. They are also leeching §6Quicksilver§f from the ground. As such, their §dSaplings§f can only be planted in locations with §6Cinnabar §fnearby. The price for growing them is a steady stream of Mercurial goodness from breaking the leaves.

Noone wants to manually craft the exact flavor of conveyor or logic gate they need at the moment.

Enter:§d The Chisel§f.
Not Only can it be used to chisel stone in the ground using left-click, but opening up its GUI and inserting an item allows you to pick the variant you want. should you ever make to much of one kind, you can just put it back in and re-chisel it.
§4§fNeither me nor §4Velvet §fhave ever seen a mineral quite like this. It looks like it is naturally luminescent, but rough scans indicate litle to no radioactivity. Can you get some for us?

Dreams, huh? Well, I'm quite the daydreamer and shower thought-haver myself, but this is something different. I'm the last person to believe in visions, but it doesn't hurt to try emulate what you saw, right?

With Flux secured, we can start thinking about some more industrial materials. Concrete is a good start.

Usually, concrete is made from aggregate, a gravel/sand mixture. if that's too inconvenient for you however, just using gravel also works, albeit at a less efficient rate.

Wow, this salis mundus stuff is versatile to be sure. I wonder what we can do with this new Crucible of yours...

Now that i think about it, I want one too!
No Description

Oh my, these flowers and devices don't appear to come with brains pre-installed, do they?
Well, now that we have access to redstone, this shouldn't be too much of a hassle. Simply Build their Brains for them using §dRedstone Logic! §f

Most Components can be interacted with through redstone. For instance, most containers like chests or Wooden Hoppers can have their contents read by a §dComparator§f and mana spreaders can be disabled by applying a signal.

The §dBarrel §fis a device capable of performing simple fluid recipes. 

Most recipes take time to complete, during which the lid must be sealed. This can simply be done by applying a redstone signal.
No Description

huh, so it turns out you can just get iron alchemically like this.
I'll have to go tell §6Izawa§f at once!
No Description
No Description

The Grindstone will be your most basic way of crushing things like redstone ore. Right-click the item to be processed on it and click some more until done. Extract the finished product using shift-click.



§cThe Quern has been replaced by this because somehow this one was more automatable. 

§f

While mining you will have to be aware of collapses, these occur when mining unsupported stone, or when causing explosions nearby. Note that ore blocks are exempt from collapses.

However a sturdy arch of wooden support beams should be able to support about 8 meters of mineshaft in each horizontal direction.
To form a minimum viable support structure, place 2 columns of at least 3 support beams 1 block apart and connect them by clicking on one of them with another beam. §6Only the horizontal beams count towards protection.

You don't have much education in geology do you? I can give a basic rundown on what you need to know.

Underground ore veins will be your main source of useful metals and minerals, however due to being underground you can't exactly spot them easily.
However surface samples typically indicate that there's ores below, just dig straight down as nothing bad ever comes of that right?
Every now and then, you will stumble across wild crops that can be harvested for produce and seeds.§6 The seeds might be useful for other things than farming, too.

§dRedstone§r is an essential material for technology, and as we want to automate stuff your probably gonna have to get it as fast as possible.
It can be primarily obtained from §dCinnabar§r and §dCryolite§r.

§dQuicksilver§r and §dRedstone§r as surface samples will both signify a redstone bearing vein bellow.
Collins told me you have successfully synthesized something called "Liquid Death". I wonder how well suited it'll be for use with your Chemthrower?

Cooking things is one of the most fundamental ways of processing. You can create a Firepit by using a §dFirestarter§f on 3 sticks and a log dropped on the ground.

The firepit can be turned into an automatable version of itself by shift-clicking on it with an empty hand.

§cFirepits and other TFC devices like it will keep consuming fuel even if the chunks aren't loaded. if you automate them, keep a supply of firestarters, flint and steel, or fire charges ready.

Torches are very simple to make, just light some sticks on fire! 

Keep in mind that they will burn out after 3 days and will have to be re-lit, so it would be best to look into alternative sources of lighting.

If you look to the right in your inventory, there should be 4 new tabs. the lowest one is your §6Nutrition§f, spllit between dairy, fruit, grain, vegetables, and protein. The lower your overall nutrition, the lower your effective max health. 

For Nutrition, only the last 20 foods count toward it. if you want to maximize your health pool, it is advised to use meals like sandwiches or stews. the former is created in a crafting table using bread while the latter is made in a §dCeramic Pot §fover a Firepit.

The pictures you sent show some ancient machinery and crates. I suggest salvaging them using a §dCrowbar§f and §dHammer§f*. To know which tool is needed for which part, hover over them. the more rectangular tool is the hammer while the more hoe-shaped symbol indicates a crowbar.

Some of the still useable machinery might require you to calibrate some switches. 

For the pumpjack/ extractor looking things, I suggest you plug a non-full §dThermal Cell §finto it and fiddle with the settings until the machine comes to life. Before wasting your time with that, though, make sure it actually has power. From what i could discern, some have pipes that glow orange while others do not.

*Bring the best Hammer you have. I don't think anything less than an Iron one will be enough.

It is worth noting that§6 Fortune on Crowbar and Hammer works wonders for getting more of the components back.

To make charcoal, put piles of logs (shift-click while placing logs) in an airtight space and light it on fire. When the smoke particles subside, it's safe to dig up.

To form a charcoal forge, place 7-8 charcoal in a 1x1 hole surrounded by stone* and light it. As with the firepit, it can be shift-clicked to make a more automatable version with item I/O.

*Anything made of stone will work. Even things like mechanical users and droppers.

Despite what certain outdated forms of documentation may tell you, the §6Coke Oven§f is now built using §dFire Bricks§f.

Also, any old smithing hammer will do for assembling it. No need for fancy engineer's tools.

The Coke Oven allows for refining of bituminous coal, lignite or peat into §6Coal Coke§f, a better, but still lackluster Solid Fuel. It also produces §6Creosote Oil§f which can be used as a basic liquid fuel. It also provides a better ratio and Creosote Byproduct for Turning logs into §6Charcoal§f.

This pearticular flower seems to delight in consuming flammable materials. I could have used that info *before* it ate through half of my Coat, but here we are. 

Generating flowers have to be placed next to a mana spreader in order to work, or be bound to one afterwards via a wand of the forest or similar.

§6I suspect that burnable fuel comes at a premium to you right now. Perhaps start looking into alternative sources of Mana.

The §dChemthrower §fis perhaps the most overkill weapon in your arsenal right now. Fed with the right ammunition, it can deal ludicrous amounts of damage in an area. 

The Price you pay is of course that it guzzles Fuel like there is no tomorrow.

a §dReservoir§f might be able to alleviate any storage space concerns at least: Acting effectively like an upgraded jerrycan, they can be "activated" with shift-click. any fluid you put in it will automatically be transferred to held items.
The Gauntlet you've devised makes for a great weapon when combined with the right foci.
In order to be able to defend yourself efficiently, you must know what options are vailable to you. This will be a non-exhaustive list, but i think it should cover the most interesting options.
As your sphere of influence expands, it becomes simply infeasible to patrol your base's perimeter all on your own. Instead, consider fortifying it with some Turrets! Here's some I've been able to

Possibly the simplest kind of Turret there is, using common arrows as ammunition. 

It can grab arrows from a dropper below itself to refill.
You can also make it ride minecarts, so you can have one defense train for sections that only need infrequent sweeps.

§cArrow collisions have been modified such that they do not happen if a minecart or Turret are nearby. Effectively, this means that Crossbow Turrets will not engage in friendly fire and can be placed in greater numbers and even on Trains!*

*sometimes when going on a very specific angle it may still destroy minecarts. beware of adding unnecessary slopes if you use this.

betterquesting:10.desc:8: The §dMinigun §fIs a fast-firing weapon that must be charged with compressed air and up to 4 magazines. It sports a wide-ish variety of ammo types, like incendiary, AP, HE, and freezing.
This Turret runs on Minigun Ammunition and cannot be targeted by hostiles. You can increase its range using upgrades.

However, they usually also bring with them new machinery that can only be set up there. Now i'm not §6Izawa §for §bCollins§f, but i predict that §6Setting up processing lines across different worlds will prove indispensable.

The scanners have picked up unnaturally large quantities of refined metal below Mountains and High Hills. Get your caving gear, because it's basically at the very bottom of the world. Also bring your best armor. who knows what the creatures this far down are like.

A couple dozen blocks underground, you might be able to find abandoned mineshafts. What they were digging up i do not know. Definitely not the readily available metals and other ore deposits you can find just exposed in the walls.

Hello there, I'm §4Dr. Alice Velvet §fand I am here to teach you about the basics of surviving on an alien planet! I hope a geology degree and my meager carpentry skills will suffice in helping you not die.

§6§aCorporal Logan§f reporting for Duty! I'm from supply chain management and have just been, uh, prematurely promoted to head of logistics.
If you have any deliveries to make or need help with getting things where they need to be, come to §mus§f me.

You know what they say: an engineer's job is not done whennothing more can be added, but when nothing more can be removed. Did not think i'd ever have to design around removing... all of technology as we know it, 
but nothing you and renowned mechanical Engineer §6Dr. Izawa§f can't solve if we put our
heads together, right?

Hello there! I'm §bQuinn Collins§f, Particle Physicist and Spatial Technician. Or at least that's what is on my diploma.
Since I doubt that we'll be taking a closer look at warp drives or colliders anytime soon, I'm basically sitting on my hands right now.

Maybe my colleagues will find §5something§f they need my help explaining...

This is §1Dr. Cave Dave Weller §freporting from the Comms Bridge! The sensors are... in bad shape and we have considerable interference, but I think we'll manage. Let's familiarize ourselves with our surroundings, shall we?

Name's §5Dr. Xavier§f, Sociologist and Tactical Xenobiologist. 

Or in other words, I show our soldiers what body parts to shoot at and how to destroy enemy morale. 
Let's hope this next mission includes a little less violence.

§7Lieutenant Briggs§f here. I have served on many a military vessel, faced countless alien threats. And through It all, there was only one thing that protected me. Gun. And if that didn't work, we got more Gun.
